item.title: Explainable Anomaly Detection in Noisy Web Corpora
item.description: We present a hybrid anomaly detection method for noisy web corpora that combines rule-based filters with statistical z-score tests and TF-IDF centroid distance. Each detected anomaly receives a natural-language explanation, which improves reviewer trust in data cleaning pipelines for machine learning training data. Experiments on crawled feed datasets show a substantial reduction in false positives compared to rules alone.

item.title: Weak Supervision for Topic Labeling of Technical News Feeds
item.description: We study weak supervision strategies for assigning topic labels to technical news feeds without manual annotation. Keyword rules, source metadata and confidence weights are combined to produce a labeled dataset suitable for training a text classifier. We analyze label noise, class imbalance and the effect of cleaning steps on downstream model quality.

item.title: Respectful Crawling: Lessons from Robots Exclusion Protocol Compliance
item.description: Large language model training increasingly relies on web data. We measure how well crawlers comply with the Robots Exclusion Protocol (RFC 9309), analyze crawl-delay usage and quantify the legal and ethical risks of ignoring terms of service. We propose a compliance checklist for dataset builders who collect public feeds.

item.title: A Survey of Text Deduplication Methods for Training Corpora
item.description: Duplicate and near-duplicate documents degrade the quality of machine learning datasets. We survey exact hashing, MinHash and SimHash approaches, compare their precision and recall on web-scale corpora, and discuss practical trade-offs in memory usage and compute cost for data engineering pipelines.

item.title: Tokenization Artifacts and Dataset Quality in Low-Resource Languages
item.description: We investigate how tokenization artifacts affect the quality of datasets for low-resource languages. Broken encodings, mojibake and inconsistent normalization introduce noise that harms neural model training. We propose automated quality checks that flag such anomalies before dataset release.
